docs.title: OAuth 2.0 for React Client
docs.text:
The DTaaS React client website authorises users with the OAuth 2.0 PKCE authorisation flow. The setup steps are:

1. Choose a GitLab Server:

  • OAuth 2.0 authorisation must be set up on a GitLab server. An on-premises GitLab installation is preferable to the commercial https://gitlab.com.
  • The GitLab Omnibus Docker can be used for this purpose.
  • The OAuth 2.0 application should be configured as an instance-wide authorization type.

2. Determine the Website's Hostname:

  • Decide the hostname of the website before setting up OAuth on GitLab. A self-hosted GitLab instance is recommended, because other parts of the DTaaS platform use it too.

3. Define Callback and Logout URLs:

  • For the PKCE authorisation flow to function correctly, two URLs are required: a callback URL and a logout URL.
  • The callback URL tells the OAuth 2.0 provider where to redirect signed-in users. It differs from the landing homepage of the DTaaS platform.
  • The logout URL is where users go after logging out.

4. OAuth 2.0 Application Creation:

  • During the creation of the OAuth 2.0 application on GitLab, the scope must be specified. The openid, profile, read_user, read_repository, and api scopes should be selected.

5. Application ID:

  • After successfully creating the OAuth 2.0 application, GitLab generates an application ID. This long hexadecimal string is needed in the configuration files.

6. Required Information from OAuth 2.0 Application:

  • The following information from the OAuth 2.0 application registered on GitLab is required:
GitLab Variable Name Variable Name in Client env.js Default Value OAuth 2.0 Provider REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY https://gitlab.intocps.org/ Application ID REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID Callback URL REACT_APP_REDIRECT_URI https://intocps.org/Library Scopes REACT_APP_GITLAB_SCOPES openid, profile, read_user, read_repository, api

7. Create User Accounts:

User accounts must be created in GitLab for all usernames chosen during installation. The server deployment packages use two default usernames, user1 and user2. Create GitLab accounts for whichever usernames your installation uses.

docs.title: Username claim resolution for OIDC providers
docs.text:
DTaaS resolves the logged-in username from common OIDC claims, so it works with several providers (for example GitLab, Keycloak and Dex).

The client checks claims in this order:

  1. preferred_username
  2. username
  3. nickname
  4. login
  5. local part of email (before @)
  6. local part of upn (before @)
  7. last path segment of profile URL (GitLab-compatible fallback)
  8. sub

This order preserves existing GitLab behavior while allowing providers that do not expose profile URLs to authenticate correctly.

The resolved username is restricted to a URL-path-safe character set (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ @ + -, and never the .. sequence). A claim that does not match is skipped in favour of the next claim in the order above. The check exists because the username is later used, unencoded, as a path segment in backend GitLab URLs (see below).

docs.title: Provider support versus backend account requirements
docs.text:
The sign-in steps above are written for GitLab because the rest of the DTaaS platform (workspaces, digital twins, libraries) relies on a GitLab instance. The username resolution itself works with any OIDC provider that issues one of the claims listed above (for example Keycloak, Dex or GitHub).

Authenticating with a non-GitLab provider only signs the user into the website. Backend features also require that the resolved username matches an existing account (namespace) on the configured GitLab instance, because requests are constructed as {gitlab}/{group}/{username}/-/raw/.... If no GitLab account with that username exists, sign-in succeeds but GitLab-backed operations fail. Administrators using an external identity provider must therefore keep the provider usernames aligned with the GitLab usernames.

docs.title: Configure Client Website
docs.text:
This page describes the configuration options for the React website. The options are set in env.js, which defines window.env.

if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  window.env = {
    REACT_APP_ENVIRONMENT: "prod | dev | local | test",
    REACT_APP_URL: "URL for the gateway",
    REACT_APP_URL_BASENAME: "Base URL for the client website"(optional, can be null),
    REACT_APP_URL_DTLINK: "Endpoint for the Digital Twin",
    REACT_APP_URL_LIBLINK: "Endpoint for the Library Assets",
    REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID: 'AppID generated by the GitLab OAuth 2.0 provider',
    REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY: 'URL of the private GitLab instance',
    REACT_APP_REDIRECT_URI: 'URL of the homepage for the logged in users of the website',
    REACT_APP_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI: 'URL of the homepage for the anonymous users of the website',
    REACT_APP_GITLAB_SCOPES: 'OAuth 2.0 scopes. These should match with the scopes set in GitLab OAuth 2.0 provider',
    LOGGER_URL: 'Endpoint of the logger microservice, including the /logger prefix'(optional),
  };
};

// Example values with no base URL. Trailing and ending slashes are optional.
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  window.env = {
    REACT_APP_ENVIRONMENT: 'prod',
    REACT_APP_URL: 'https://intocps.org/',
    REACT_APP_URL_BASENAME: '',
    REACT_APP_URL_DTLINK: '/lab',
    REACT_APP_URL_LIBLINK: '',

    REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID: '1be55736756190b3ace4c2c4fb19bde386d1dcc748d20b47ea8cfb5935b8446c',
    REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY: 'https://gitlab.intocps.org/',
    REACT_APP_REDIRECT_URI: 'https://intocps.org/Library',
    REACT_APP_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI: 'https://intocps.org/',
    REACT_APP_GITLAB_SCOPES: 'openid profile read_user read_repository api',
    LOGGER_URL: 'https://intocps.org/logger',
  };
};


// Example values with "bar" as basename URL.
//Trailing and ending slashes are optional.
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  window.env = {
    REACT_APP_ENVIRONMENT: "dev",
    REACT_APP_URL: 'http://localhost:4000/',
    REACT_APP_URL_BASENAME: 'bar',
    REACT_APP_URL_DTLINK: '/lab',
    REACT_APP_URL_LIBLINK: '',

    REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID: '1be55736756190b3ace4c2c4fb19bde386d1dcc748d20b47ea8cfb5935b8446c',
    REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY: 'https://gitlab.intocps.org/',
    REACT_APP_REDIRECT_URI: 'http://localhost:4000/bar/Library',
    REACT_APP_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI: 'http://localhost:4000/bar',
    REACT_APP_GITLAB_SCOPES: 'openid profile read_user read_repository api',
  };
};

REACT_APP_GITLAB_SCOPES must be exactly openid profile read_user read_repository api; the client rejects any other value when it checks the configuration.

LOGGER_URL is optional. Workflow logging and remote logging are off by default, and users turn them on in their account settings. When LOGGER_URL is empty or missing, enabled logging keeps events in the browser (IndexedDB). When LOGGER_URL is set and remote logging is on, the configuration check requests <LOGGER_URL>/health.

docs.title: config/conf.server - Traefik Forward-Auth Rules
docs.text:
Source: config/conf.server.example

This file defines per-path authorisation rules for traefik-forward-auth. Each rule restricts a URL path to specific email addresses.

cp config/conf.server.example config/conf.server

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
rule.<NAME>.action=auth
rule.<NAME>.rule=PathPrefix(`/<path>`)
rule.<NAME>.whitelist=<email>

docs.title: Default Rules
docs.text:
rule.libms.action=auth
rule.libms.rule=PathPrefix(`/lib`)

rule.onlyu1.action=auth
rule.onlyu1.rule=PathPrefix(`/user1`)
rule.onlyu1.whitelist=user1@emailservice.com

rule.onlyu2.action=auth
rule.onlyu2.rule=PathPrefix(`/user2`)
rule.onlyu2.whitelist=user2@emailservice.com

Replace the usernames and email addresses with those of the actual users.

docs.title: Important Rules
docs.text:
• Usernames in config/.env (USERNAME1, USERNAME2) must match PathPrefix values in config/conf.server.
  • If a route exists in docker-compose.yml but has no rule in config/conf.server, any signed-in user can open it.
  • If a rule exists in config/conf.server but no router serves that path, the URL returns 404.

certs/

\- privkey.pem     # Private key

The certificates must be valid for SERVER_DNS.

files/

cp -R files/template files/<USERNAME>

docs.title: OAuth 2.0 Application Setup
docs.text: The external GitLab instance needs two OAuth 2.0 applications.

docs.title: DTaaS Client Authorization (React Frontend)
docs.text:
1. In GitLab, open Applications.
  2. Create an application:
  3. Name: DTaaS Client Authorization
  4. Redirect URI: https://<SERVER_DNS>/Library
  5. Confidential: unticked (public SPA client)
  6. Scopes: openid, profile, read_user, read_repository, api
  7. Save the Application ID and set REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID in config/client.js.
  8. Set REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY in config/client.js to the GitLab URL.

docs.title: DTaaS Server Authorization (Traefik Forward-Auth)
docs.text:
1. In GitLab, create another application:
  2. Name: DTaaS Server Authorization
  3. Redirect URI: https://<SERVER_DNS>/_oauth
  4. Confidential: ticked
  5. Scopes: read_user
  6. Save the Application ID and Secret.
  7. Set OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET and OAUTH_URL in config/.env.
  8. Generate OAUTH_SECRET and set it in config/.env.

docs.title: Reload After Configuration
docs.text: docker compose --env-file config/.env up -d --force-recreate client traefik-forward-auth

docs.title: Adding More Users
docs.text:
To add a third user:

  1. Add a user3 service to docker-compose.yml, modelled on user1 and user2.
  2. Add USERNAME3=<name> to config/.env.
  3. Create the files/<name> directory from files/template.
  4. Add a matching authorisation rule to config/conf.server.
  5. Restart:
docker compose --env-file config/.env up -d

docs.title: Authentication redirect loop
docs.text:
• Check OAUTH_URL in config/.env.
  • Check REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY in config/client.js.
  • Clear the browser cookies for the domain.
  • Check the logs:
docker compose --env-file config/.env logs traefik-forward-auth

docs.title: 404 on user workspace
docs.text:
• Check that the usernames are the same in:
  • config/.env
  • config/conf.server
  • docker-compose.yml

docs.title: TLS warning in browser
docs.text: • Replace certs/fullchain.pem and certs/privkey.pem with valid certificates.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This package deploys DTaaS with Traefik, OAuth forward-auth and two user workspaces.

A path such as /user1 is the URL route of that service, for example https://intocps.org/user1. The thick arrow is the forward-auth check: Traefik asks traefik-forward-auth to authorise each request before it routes it.

The docker-compose.yml starts the following services:

Service Purpose traefik Reverse proxy with TLS termination client DTaaS React frontend logger-ms Logger microservice user1 / user2 JupyterLab user workspaces libms Library management microservice traefik-forward-auth OAuth 2.0 authorisation middleware

| - logs/                                                                  |
| \- logger/             # Logger microservice events                      |
| - docker-compose.yml     # Service definitions                           |
| - CONFIG.md              # Detailed configuration reference              |
\- README.md              # This file

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
This page describes every configuration file in this package. For the quick-start installation guide, see install.md.

Important

This guide uses the hostname intocps.org as an example. Replace it with the hostname of your server.

docs.title: config/.env - Docker Compose Environment
docs.text:
Source: config/.env.example

This file holds the environment variables that docker-compose.yml reads.

cp config/.env.example config/.env

docs.title: Server Settings
docs.text: Variable Example Description SERVER_DNS intocps.org Domain name or IP address of the server. Do not include https://. USERNAME1 user1 Path prefix and workspace name for the first user USERNAME2 user2 Path prefix and workspace name for the second user COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME dtaas Docker Compose project name (rarely needs changing)

docs.title: OAuth 2.0 Settings
docs.text:
Fill these in after the GitLab instance is running and the OAuth 2.0 applications exist (see OAuth 2.0 Application Setup).

Variable Example Description OAUTH_URL https://intocps.org/gitlab GitLab instance URL used for browser-side authorisation redirects. No trailing slash. OAUTH_CLIENT_ID (from GitLab) Application ID from the DTaaS Server Authorization OAuth 2.0 application OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET (from GitLab) Secret from the DTaaS Server Authorization OAuth 2.0 application OAUTH_SECRET (random string) Encryption key for OAuth session cookies. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32

docs.title: How Variables Map to Services
docs.text:
Variable Used by SERVER_DNS client, logger-ms, user1, user2, libms, traefik-forward-auth, gitlab USERNAME1 / USERNAME2 user1, user2 (routing and workspace volumes) OAUTH_URL traefik-forward-auth (browser redirect URL) OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET traefik-forward-auth OAUTH_SECRET traefik-forward-auth

traefik-forward-auth reaches the token and user endpoints over the internal Docker network (http://gitlab/gitlab/...), so only the authorisation redirect uses OAUTH_URL.

docs.title: config/client.js - DTaaS Web Client
docs.text:
Source: config/client.js.example

This JavaScript file is mounted into the React client container and configures the DTaaS web application at runtime.

cp config/client.js.example config/client.js

docs.title: Variable Reference
docs.text: Variable Example Description REACT_APP_ENVIRONMENT prod Environment name. Use prod for production. REACT_APP_URL https://intocps.org Base URL of the DTaaS web application REACT_APP_URL_BASENAME '' Optional URL base path (leave empty for root hosting) REACT_APP_URL_DTLINK /lab URL path for the Digital Twin workbench REACT_APP_URL_LIBLINK '' URL path for the Library REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID (from GitLab) Application ID from the DTaaS Client Authorization OAuth 2.0 application REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY https://intocps.org/gitlab URL of the GitLab instance (OAuth 2.0 issuer) REACT_APP_REDIRECT_URI https://intocps.org/Library Where GitLab sends users after sign-in REACT_APP_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI https://intocps.org/ Where users land after sign-out REACT_APP_GITLAB_SCOPES openid profile read_user read_repository api OAuth 2.0 scopes requested during sign-in LOGGER_URL https://intocps.org/logger URL of the logger service

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  window.env = {
    REACT_APP_ENVIRONMENT: 'prod',
    REACT_APP_URL: 'https://intocps.org',
    REACT_APP_URL_BASENAME: '',
    REACT_APP_URL_DTLINK: '/lab',
    REACT_APP_URL_LIBLINK: '',
    REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID: '<APPLICATION_ID>',
    REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY: 'https://intocps.org/gitlab',
    REACT_APP_REDIRECT_URI: 'https://intocps.org/Library',
    REACT_APP_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI: 'https://intocps.org/',
    REACT_APP_GITLAB_SCOPES: 'openid profile read_user read_repository api',
    LOGGER_URL: 'https://intocps.org/logger',
  };
};

docs.title: config/conf.server - Traefik Forward-Auth Rules
docs.text:
Source: config/conf.server.example

This file defines per-path authorisation rules for traefik-forward-auth. Each rule restricts a URL path to specific GitLab email addresses.

cp config/conf.server.example config/conf.server

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
rule.<NAME>.action=auth
rule.<NAME>.rule=PathPrefix(`/<path>`)
rule.<NAME>.whitelist=<email>

docs.title: Default Rules
docs.text:
rule.libms.action=auth
rule.libms.rule=PathPrefix(`/lib`)

rule.onlyu1.action=auth
rule.onlyu1.rule=PathPrefix(`/user1`)
rule.onlyu1.whitelist=user1@emailservice.com

rule.onlyu2.action=auth
rule.onlyu2.rule=PathPrefix(`/user2`)
rule.onlyu2.whitelist=user2@emailservice.com

Replace user1, user2 and the email addresses with those of the actual GitLab accounts.

docs.title: Important Rules
docs.text:
Warning

The usernames in config/.env (USERNAME1, USERNAME2) must match the PathPrefix values in config/conf.server. A mismatch causes routing or authorisation failures.

Scenario Behaviour Route in config/.env but missing from config/conf.server Any signed-in user can access the route (default forward-auth behaviour) Route in config/conf.server but missing from config/.env Traefik returns 404 (route not served) The /lib rule has no whitelist Any signed-in user can access the library service

docs.title: certs/ - TLS Certificates
docs.text:
Place the TLS certificate files here:

certs/
├── fullchain.pem   # Public certificate (or certificate chain)
└── privkey.pem     # Private key

The certificates must be valid for SERVER_DNS (e.g. intocps.org or *.intocps.org).

To obtain certificates with certbot:

# Using certbot (Let's Encrypt)
sudo certbot certonly --standalone -d intocps.org
sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/intocps.org/fullchain.pem certs/
sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/intocps.org/privkey.pem   certs/

If the certificate files are absent or invalid, Traefik uses self-signed certificates and browsers show a security warning.

docs.title: files/ - User Workspace Directories
docs.text:
Each user workspace container mounts a directory from files/ as its /workspace volume. All workspaces share the files/common/ directory, which is mounted at /workspace/common in each container.

files/
├── common/    # Shared files (mounted to /workspace/common in each container)
└── template/  # template workspace files

Create a directory for each user:

cp -R files/template files/<USERNAME>
sudo chown -R 1000:100 files/*

UID 1000 and GID 100 match the default user inside the workspace container.

docs.title: logs/logger/ - Logger Microservice Events
docs.text:
The logger microservice writes the captured events to logs/logger/workflow-logs.jsonl. Create the directory and give it to uid 1000, the user that runs the logger:

mkdir -p logs/logger
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 logs/logger

logs/ itself holds the GitLab logs, so change the owner of logs/logger only.

docs.title: OAuth 2.0 Application Setup
docs.text: Once the GitLab instance is running, register two OAuth 2.0 applications to connect DTaaS and Traefik forward-auth to the integrated GitLab.

docs.title: DTaaS Client Authorization (React Frontend)
docs.text:
1. In GitLab, go to Admin Area → Applications (or the user's Edit Profile → Applications).
  2. Create a new application:
  3. Name: DTaaS Client Authorization
  4. Redirect URI: https://intocps.org/Library
  5. Confidential: unticked (public SPA client)
  6. Scopes: openid, profile, read_user, read_repository, api
  7. Save the Application ID.
  8. Set REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID in config/client.js to this Application ID.
  9. Set REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY in config/client.js to https://intocps.org/gitlab.

For details, see the client auth documentation.

docs.title: DTaaS Server Authorization (Traefik Forward-Auth)
docs.text:
1. In GitLab, go to Admin Area → Applications.
  2. Create a new application:
  3. Name: DTaaS Server Authorization
  4. Redirect URI: https://intocps.org/_oauth
  5. Confidential: ticked
  6. Scopes: read_user
  7. Save the Application ID and Secret.
  8. Set OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET in config/.env.
  9. Set OAUTH_URL in config/.env to https://intocps.org/gitlab.
  10. Generate OAUTH_SECRET with openssl rand -base64 32 and set it in config/.env.

For details, see the server auth documentation.

docs.title: Reload After Configuration
docs.text:
After putting the OAuth 2.0 credentials into the configuration files, reload the affected services:

docker compose --env-file config/.env up -d --force-recreate client traefik-forward-auth

docs.title: Adding More Users
docs.text:
To add a third user:

  1. Add a service to docker-compose.yml:
user3:
  image: intocps/workspace:main-56c6f68
  restart: unless-stopped
  environment:
    - MAIN_USER=${USERNAME3:-user3}
  volumes:
    - "./files/common:/workspace/common"
    - "./files/${USERNAME3:-user3}:/workspace"
  labels:
    - "traefik.enable=true"
    - "traefik.http.routers.u3.rule=Host(`${SERVER_DNS:-localhost}`) && PathPrefix(`/${USERNAME3:-user3}`)"
    - "traefik.http.routers.u3.tls=true"
    - "traefik.http.routers.u3.middlewares=traefik-forward-auth"
  networks:
    - users
  1. Add to config/.env:
USERNAME3=alice
  1. Create the workspace directory:
cp -R files/template files/alice
sudo chown -R 1000:100 files/alice
  1. Add an authorisation rule to config/conf.server:
rule.onlyu3.action=auth
rule.onlyu3.rule=PathPrefix(`/alice`)
rule.onlyu3.whitelist=alice@emailservice.com

  1. Create a GitLab account for alice in the integrated GitLab instance.

  2. Restart:

docker compose --env-file config/.env up -d

docs.title: GitLab Takes Too Long to Start
docs.text: GitLab CE needs substantial resources, and the first startup can take 5 to 10 minutes. Follow progress with docker compose --env-file config/.env logs -f gitlab. Make sure the host has at least 4 GB of RAM available for GitLab.

docs.title: Authentication Redirect Loop
docs.text:
1. Check that OAUTH_URL in config/.env matches the URL that the user's browser can reach (e.g. https://intocps.org/gitlab).
  2. Check that REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY in config/client.js matches the same URL.
  3. Clear the browser cookies for the domain.
  4. Check the traefik-forward-auth logs: docker compose --env-file config/.env logs traefik-forward-auth

docs.title: 404 on User Workspace
docs.text:
• Make sure USERNAME1/USERNAME2 in config/.env match the PathPrefix values in config/conf.server.
  • Make sure a matching service exists in docker-compose.yml.

docs.title: GitLab "502 Bad Gateway"
docs.text: GitLab is still initialising. Wait until docker ps shows the container as healthy.

docs.title: Self-Signed Certificate Warning in Browser
docs.text: The TLS certificate files in certs/ are missing or invalid. Replace them with valid certificates for the domain.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
This guide installs a secure, multi-user DTaaS deployment that uses an integrated GitLab instance for OAuth 2.0 authorisation.

Download dtaas-secure-server-integrated-gitlab-xx.zip from the latest release / pre-release page.

For the configuration reference, see config.md.

Important

This guide uses the hostname intocps.org as an example. Replace it with the hostname of your server.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This package installs DTaaS as a multi-user web application with an integrated GitLab CE instance. GitLab is both the OAuth 2.0 authorisation provider and the DevOps backend for digital twin projects.

A path such as /user1 is the URL route of that service, for example https://intocps.org/user1. The thick arrow is the forward-auth check: Traefik asks traefik-forward-auth to authorise each request before it routes it.

The docker-compose.yml starts the following services:

Service Purpose traefik Reverse proxy with TLS termination client DTaaS React frontend logger-ms Logger microservice user1 / user2 JupyterLab user workspaces libms Library management microservice traefik-forward-auth OAuth 2.0 authorisation middleware gitlab Integrated GitLab CE (OAuth 2.0 provider)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Requirement Details Docker Engine v28 or later with Compose plugin Domain name A domain name (e.g. intocps.org) or IP address TLS certificate fullchain.pem and privkey.pem for the domain. Obtain via certbot or a certificate provider

docs.title: 1. Create Configuration Files
docs.text:
cp config/.env.example       config/.env
cp config/conf.server.example config/conf.server
cp config/client.js.example     config/client.js

Edit config/.env and set SERVER_DNS, USERNAME1 and USERNAME2. Leave the OAUTH_* variables as placeholders for now; you fill them in once the GitLab instance is running (see step 5).

See config.md for a reference of every variable.

docs.title: 2. Create User Workspace Directories
docs.text:
cp -R files/template files/<USERNAME1>
cp -R files/template files/<USERNAME2>
sudo chown -R 1000:100 files/*

The logger microservice writes its events to logs/logger. Create the directory and give it to uid 1000, the user that runs the logger:

mkdir -p logs/logger
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 logs/logger

logs/ itself holds the GitLab logs, so change the owner of logs/logger only.

docs.title: 3. Add TLS Certificates
docs.text:
cp /path/to/fullchain.pem certs/fullchain.pem
cp /path/to/privkey.pem   certs/privkey.pem

Traefik falls back to self-signed certificates if these files are absent or invalid.

docs.title: 4. Start Services
docs.text:
docker compose --env-file config/.env up -d

GitLab takes a few minutes to become healthy. Watch its status with:

watch docker ps

docs.title: 5. Configure GitLab
docs.text:
Once the GitLab container shows as healthy:

  1. Log in to https://intocps.org/gitlab as root. The initial password is in config/gitlab/initial_root_password.

    Warning

    GitLab deletes this file 24 hours after the first start. Save the password immediately.

  2. Create user accounts (see GitLab docs). The usernames must match USERNAME1/USERNAME2 in config/.env.

  3. Register two OAuth 2.0 applications in GitLab (Admin Area → Applications):

  4. DTaaS Client Authorization for the React SPA frontend. See the client auth docs.

  5. DTaaS Server Authorization for the Traefik forward-auth backend. See the server auth docs.

  6. Put the generated OAuth 2.0 credentials into the configuration files:

  7. Set REACT_APP_CLIENT_ID and REACT_APP_AUTH_AUTHORITY in config/client.js.

  8. Set OAUTH_URL, OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET in config/.env.

  9. Update the user permissions in config/conf.server.

  10. Reload the services:

docker compose --env-file config/.env up -d --force-recreate client traefik-forward-auth

docs.title: 6. Verify
docs.text: URL Expected result https://intocps.org DTaaS web interface (redirects to GitLab sign-in) https://intocps.org/gitlab Integrated GitLab instance https://intocps.org/user1 User 1 workspace (after sign-in) https://intocps.org/user2 User 2 workspace (after sign-in)

docs.title: Stop
docs.text: docker compose --env-file config/.env down

docs.title: Directory Layout
docs.text:
.
├── certs/                 # TLS certificates (fullchain.pem, privkey.pem)
├── config/
│   ├── .env               # Docker compose environment variables
│   ├── conf.server        # Traefik forward-auth authorisation rules
│   ├── client.js          # DTaaS React client configuration
│   ├── gitlab/            # GitLab config (mounted as /etc/gitlab)
│   └── tls.yml            # Traefik TLS provider configuration
├── data/                  # GitLab persistent data (/var/opt/gitlab)
├── files/
│   ├── common/            # Shared files across all workspaces
│   └── template/          # sample user workspace files
├── logs/                  # GitLab logs (/var/log/gitlab)
│   └── logger/            # Logger microservice events
├── docker-compose.yml     # Service definitions
├── CONFIG.md              # Detailed configuration reference
└── README.md              # This file — quick-start guide

docs.title: References
docs.text: Image sources: Traefik logo, GitLab

docs.title: GitLab Server
docs.text: DTaaS supports two ways of installing a local GitLab instance.

docs.title: Option A: Integrated DTaaS Package
docs.text:
A path such as /user1 is the URL route of that service, for example https://intocps.org/user1. The thick arrow is the forward-auth check: Traefik asks traefik-forward-auth to authorise each request before it routes it.

See secure server with GitLab, then continue with the integration guide.

docs.title: Option B: Services CLI GitLab Workflow
docs.text:
Server 1 runs DTaaS and server 2 runs GitLab. The routes and the thick arrow mean the same as in Option A.

Use the services CLI if GitLab runs as one of the platform services, then continue with the integration guide.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The DTaaS client auth authority must match the actual GitLab endpoint.
  • For integrated package deployments, use the package's own config/ files.
  • For services CLI deployments, use the files of the generated services project.

docs.text:

  • Runner setup (Linux)
  • Runner setup (Windows)
